Hi all,

I don't know if I am just doing this wrong, or I am trying to do something I should not be able to do.

The goal is to use a reactive, such as input_select, to specify the variable to use for the y-axis.

Any insights or guidance much appreciated!

Thanks,

Ian

library(ggvis)

set.seed(3.14)
n_points <- 100

x <- runif(n_points, min = -10, max = 10)
y1 <- 3 * x + 5 + rnorm(n_points, mean = 0, sd = 4)
y2 <- -2 * x - 4 + rnorm(n_points, mean = 0, sd = 4)

df <- data.frame(x, y1, y2)

# works!
df %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x, y = as.name <http://as.name>("y2")) %>%
  layer_points()

choices <- c("y1", "y2")
choices_name <- c(y1 = as.name <http://as.name>("y1"), y2 = as.name <http://as.name>("y2"))

# what is the right way to get this to work?

# error
df %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x, y = as.name <http://as.name>(input_select(choices))) %>%
  layer_points()

# error
df %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x, y = input_select(as.name <http://as.name>(choices))) %>%
  layer_points()

# error
df %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x, y = input_select(choices_name)) %>%
  layer_points()

I am trying to reactively change the sort order specification for a ggvis plot within a shiny reactive document. More broadly I am trying to force dynamic variable name selection into a ggvis specification, but ...

The static code:

library(ggplot2)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

diamonds%>%
  group_by(color)%>%
  ggvis(x=~carat, y=~price)%>%
  layer_points(fill=~color)%>%
  layer_smooths(stroke=~color)

produces the expected plot.

As a next step towards making the graph reactive, I wanted to make the stratifying variable ("color" in the above example) reactive:

---
title: "Untitled"
runtime: shiny
output: html_document
---

## Inputs and Outputs

```{r}
#library(ggplot2)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)
data(diamonds)

```{r}

inputPanel(

selectInput(inputId = "varchoice", choices = names(diamonds), selected = "price", label = "Variable Choice")

)

renderPlot({

diamonds%>%
  group_by(input$varchoice)%>%
  ggvis(x=~carat, y=~price)%>%
  layer_points(fill=input$varchoice)%>%
  layer_smooths(stroke=input$varchoice)

})
```
This is the end.

The selectInput function is working as expected and produces the input box with all of the variable names from diamonds, but I then see the error: object 'input' not found .

I have tried several other variations, including casting the input$varchoice inside the as.name <http://as.name> function, but none of my efforts have been successful in moving the value input$varchoice into the graph specification in a way that is synatically correct.

I would welcome suggestions on how to dynamically change this variable.

I am optimistic that once I can change the sort order/fill/stroke variable, I will also have the insight to be able to change the X axis variable, but ... one problem at a time.

Regards,

Thanks,

messages.subject_clean: ggvis + shiny + dplyr issue with grouped data frames
messages.body_plain:
Not sure if it's better to post this on the ggvis, shiny or dplyr group but there's an issue right now with grouped data.  I have a shiny app that has a reactive data frame.  Initially the data frame is empty and contains some place holders.  Upon clicking an actionbutton this dataframe is now populated with data.  The issue is that when you group the populated dataframe, ggvis seems to still want to plot the unpopulated dataframe.  It will plot correctly if you simply remove the group_by statement or pipe in ungroup().  Although the fix is easy in the following example, some plots might require a group_by statement and this problem would be an issue.

The following is a reproducible example:

#server.R
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  rct_get_df = reactive({
    #placeholder for empty data
    df = data.frame(state = "none", potency = 0, weight = 0, month = 0, price = 0)

    #real data
    if(input$data1 > 0) df = cocaine %>% filter(weight > 50) %>% group_by(state) #%>% ungroup()
    #if you remove the group_by or add ungroup() to the above line it will display the plot properly

    df
  })

  rct_get_df %>%
    ggvis(x = ~potency, y = ~weight) %>%
    layer_points(fill = ~state) %>%
    bind_shiny("ggvis")
})

#ui.R
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    actionButton("data1", "Get Data!"),
    ggvisOutput("ggvis")
  )
))

messages.body_plain:
I solved it! And of course, the solution was way too simple as that I could have thought of that a week ago.

When you're creating a ggvis plot and intend to set a key property to later use as a tooltip, it might be a good idea to set that only in the layer you actually want to apply that tooltip to, because otherwise you'll run into problems if you later use group_by() to group your data and your original tooltip variable will… well, I don't know exactly what happened, but the TL;DR is:

     plot <- data %>% ggvis(x    = ~epnum,
                           y    = ~rating,
                           fill = ~season)
    plot <- plot %>% layer_points(key := ~tooltip, …)
    if ("Show" %in% input$btn_trendlines && var_y == "rating"){
      plot <- plot %>% layer_model_predictions(model = "lm", se = F, stroke := "black")
    }
    if ("Season" %in% input$btn_trendlines && var_y == "rating"){

      plot <- plot %>% group_by(season) %>% layer_model_predictions(model = "lm", se = F, stroke = ~season)
    }

works.

Now I only have to find out how to hide the legend for the stroke property I used for the regression lines.

Anyways, thanks to anyone reading, and a friendly hello to future people who may run into a similar issue and stumble upon this post.

Sorry, I don't think there's an easy way to do this right now. You could do it a roundabout way, though, by specifying the domains of the scales and using expand=0.

data_points <- data.frame(
  x = seq(1, 5),
  y = seq(1, 5)
)

data_rects <- data.frame(

  x = 0.8, x2 = 5.2,
  y = 0.8, y2 = 5.2

)

data.frame() %>%
  ggvis() %>%
  layer_rects(
    x = ~x, x2 = ~x2, y = ~y, y2 = ~y2,

    fill := "blue", fillOpacity := 0.2, stroke := NA,

    data = data_rects
  ) %>%
  layer_points(
    x = ~x, y = ~y,
    data = data_points
  ) %>%

  scale_numeric("x", domain = c(0.8, 5.2), expand = 0) %>%
  scale_numeric("y", domain = c(0.8, 5.2), expand = 0)

Also, I think it's not documented yet, but you can use reactives directly for the domain of a scale. In the example below, data_points is dynamic. data_rects depends on it, as does the domain of the x and y scales, so the rectangle always fits the axes.

data_points <- reactive({
  invalidateLater(2000, NULL)
  data.frame(
    x = rnorm(5),
    y = rnorm(5)
  )
})

xrange <- reactive({
  xr <- range(data_points()$x)
  xr + diff(xr) * 0.05 * c(-1, 1)
})
yrange <- reactive({
  yr <- range(data_points()$y)
  yr + diff(yr) * 0.05 * c(-1, 1)
})

data_rects <- reactive({
  data.frame(x = xrange()[1], x2 = xrange()[2],
             y = yrange()[1], y2 = yrange()[2])

})

data.frame() %>%
  ggvis() %>%
  layer_rects(
    x = ~x, x2 = ~x2, y = ~y, y2 = ~y2,

    fill := "blue", fillOpacity := 0.2, stroke := NA,

    data = data_rects
  ) %>%
  layer_points(
    x = ~x, y = ~y,
    data = data_points
  ) %>%

  scale_numeric("x", domain = xrange, expand = 0) %>%
  scale_numeric("y", domain = yrange, expand = 0)

-Winston
